sources.section: Build your own Front-end Framework / Library

summary.title: Build your own React
summary.one_liner: You learn how React works internally by rewriting a minimal version of it step by step: elements, rendering, fibers, render/commit phases, reconciliation, function components and hooks.
takeaways: React elements are plain objects with type and props; createElement just builds that object and JSX compiles to calls to it.
Rendering can be split into small units of work organized as a fiber tree, using requestIdleCallback-style loops so the browser can interrupt.
Separating a render phase (building the work-in-progress tree) from a commit phase (mutating the DOM) avoids showing incomplete UI.
Reconciliation compares the new elements against the previously committed fiber tree (via alternate) by type to decide placement, update, or deletion.
Function components have no DOM node, and useState is built by storing hooks on fibers and queuing setState actions for the next render.
summary.summary: This is a step-by-step tutorial by Rodrigo Pombo that rebuilds a simplified React (called Didact) based on React 16.8. It starts by reviewing how JSX becomes createElement calls and how DOM nodes are created, then adds a render function, a work loop with fibers, separate render and commit phases, reconciliation with effect tags, function components, and finally useState hooks. The post is self-contained, includes codesandbox examples, and ends with a list of what real React does differently and features the reader could add.
